candidateEvidence.excerpt: Microsoft AI opened a six-week public consultation on September 14 about how its future MAI models should behave.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Feedback opens today and runs for the next six weeks.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: MAI means the models developed by Microsoft AI, not every model or product Microsoft offers.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: including when deployed by Operators; it does not extend to other models simply because Microsoft uses or hosts them. It is not a complete account of the requirements or safeguards for any product or deployment, including by Microsoft.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The draft Humanist AI Code of Conduct is not being used to train models today. Microsoft plans a revised version later in 2026 to guide development from 2027 onward.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: This document, and our approach more generally, is still under development so we are not using it to train our models today. Instead, we’re sharing it broadly for public consultation. We’ll take feedback, iterate on it, and publish a revised version toward the end of the year, which we’ll use to guide our model development in 2027 and beyond.

scopeAndFreshness: Future guidance is a stated plan, not implementation now.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The proposed rules say MAI models should accept interruption, correction and shutdown, and stay within the work people authorize.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The proposed principle is that it should stop through any predefined safe-stopping procedure, rather than make your intervention harder or restart without permission.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: following any predefined, human-designed safety procedures for warnings, confirmation, or safe stopping.

scopeAndFreshness: Cancelled message is an explicitly imagined example; restart boundary additionally inspected in source: will not continue or restart after that condition is met without renewed authorization.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: Microsoft acknowledges that gap: written objectives cannot ensure the intended behavior, and building, testing and revision remain necessary.
